question: Does the candidate-novelty statistic predict the sign of the relevance gain across datasets, as it does across pool geometries within a dataset?

within_dataset.detail: METR-LA novelty .40/.60/.79 -> relevance -.0086/+.0006/+.0063; PEMS-BAY .46/.73/.95 -> -.0333/+.0117/+.0156; corr(novelty, relevance) = +.80 over six pool geometries

across_datasets.detail: corr(novelty, relevance gain) = -.328 over the six standard pools; corr(novelty, MMR gain) = -.655

interpretation: Novelty measures redundancy with the anchor, which is the mechanism that operates when the pool is manipulated inside one dataset. Across datasets other factors dominate (signal quality of the correlation structure, noise level, expert quality), so the statistic must be measured and validated per deployment rather than transferred as a dataset-level constant. The measurement protocol of the paper prescribes exactly this.
